lines.name: l1
lines.text: One red cord kept a woman alive when a city fell. Her name was Rahab, and people knew her for her sin. But she hid two of God's spies, because she believed in Him. They promised her:

lines.name: l2
lines.text: “thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window”

lines.name: l3
lines.text: That cord was the sign of the promise. Then God's army marched around her city, and on the seventh day "the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat".

lines.name: l4
lines.text: The city fell. But Rahab and her family were saved, because she trusted what they said. Hebrews gives the reason: "By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not".

lines.name: l5
lines.text: It was her faith, not her past. Matthew even names her in the family line of Jesus: "And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab". Christians see a picture in that cord: the blood of Jesus, which covers all who trust Him.

lines.name: l6
lines.text: Rahab could not hold up a wall. She only hung a cord in her window, and trusted the promise. Hang your hope on Jesus the same way.
